question: Under the proposed National Building Research Institute law, how long does an employee have to decide whether to decline the offered position after being notified?
answer:
Under the National Building Research Institute Bill, an employee has **six months from the date the offer of employment in the Institute was made** to opt out. [629/2025 §33(2)(b)]

- This applies to officers/employees of the National Building Research Organisation offered employment in the Institute. [629/2025 §33(2)(a)–(b)]

question: Under the proposed Inland Revenue amendment, from which assessment date are deductions previously claimed under sections 32, 33 or 34 of the repealed Act excluded from subsection (2)?
answer:
**Years of assessment prior to 1 April 2018** — the exclusion covers amounts already deducted under sections 32, 33 or 34 of the repealed Act for "any year of assessment prior to April 1, 2018" [022/2026 §37].

- It applies "notwithstanding that any un-deducted balance of such deduction under the repealed Act remains as at April 1, 2018" [022/2026 §37].
- The provision is new subsection (2A) inserted into section 202 of the principal enactment (Inland Revenue Act, No. 24 of 2017) [022/2026 §37].

Caveats: This is the Bill version dated 2026-03-17; no Gazette ("GS") version appears in the evidence. I have taken "assessment date" to mean year of assessment, which is the text's wording.

question: Under the proposed Microfinance and Credit Regulatory Authority law, how long does a licence issued or renewed remain in effect?
answer:
A moneylending licence issued or renewed remains valid for **one year**: it “be valid for a period of one year” [653/2025 §25(c)].

- This applies to a licence “issued under section 23 or renewed under section 24” [653/2025 §25].
- A **microfinance institution** licence is different: it “shall be issued for a period of three years” [653/2025 §32(7)].

Caveats: The Act uses separate licence periods for moneylenders and microfinance institutions.

question: How far in advance must a container depot operator lodge a renewal request before the current licence ends?
answer:
A container depot operator must submit the renewal application **not less than thirty days prior to the date of expiration** of the current licence, in the prescribed form with the prescribed renewal fee [007/2026 §6].

- This is from the Licensing of Container Depot Operators - Bill (2026-01-20) [007/2026 §6].

question: Under the proposed amendment to the Prevention of Money Laundering Act, what is the new maximum duration a freezing order may be in effect?
answer:
The amended overall maximum is **three years**, with each extension capped at **four months** (up from three months) — “shall not exceed four months” and “a period of three years” [033/2026 §9].

- The pre-confirmation police Freezing Order period is separately changed to “fourteen working days” [033/2026 §8].
- These are amendments to s.8(2)(b) of the principal Act; the evidence does not reproduce the full s.8 text, so the “overall maximum” reading is based on the replaced phrases.

question: Under the amended Telecommunication Levy law, how often is the levy calculated on the value of telecom services received?
answer:
The levy is calculated **monthly**, on the value of telecommunication services received “in respect of each month” [035/2026 §2].

- This appears in the **Telecommunication Levy (Amendment) - Bill (2026-05-06)**, which substitutes section 2 of the principal enactment [035/2026 §2].
- The levy applies to “every person receiving any telecommunication service”, at the rate in the Schedule, on the value of the supply provided by an operator or provider [035/2026 §2].

question: Under the amended Bills of Exchange Ordinance, what ways are allowed for informing a party that a bill has been refused or not paid?
answer:
Under the Bills of Exchange (Amendment) Bill, notice that a bill has been dishonoured may be given “in writing or by personal communication, or by facsimile transmission or other electronic means” [612/2025 §8].

- The electronic means must “sufficiently identify the bill” and intimate dishonour by “non-acceptance or non-payment” [612/2025 §8].
- This replaces the notice provision in section 49(5) of the principal Ordinance [612/2025 §8].

question: Under the proposed Kodhagoda Gunarathana Nahimi Foundation incorporation law, who is defined as a qualified auditor?
answer:
Under the bill, a "qualified auditor" is either an individual who is a member of the Institute of Chartered Accountants of Sri Lanka (or another institute established by law) holding a practising certificate issued by that institute's Council, or a firm of accountants whose resident partners each meet that requirement [626/2025 §11(4)].

- Accounts are audited by a qualified auditor "appointed by Auditor General in terms of Article 154 of the Constitution" [626/2025 §11(3)].
- The financial year is the calendar year [626/2025 §11(1)].

Caveats: This is the Kodhagoda Gunarathana Nahimi Foundation (Incorporation) Bill (Bill, 23 July 2025), matching the name in your question.

question: What is meant by “knowledge sharing activities” under the Sri Lanka Institute of Agriculture Act?
answer:
Under the Bill, "knowledge sharing activities" is defined in the interpretation clause as "activities designed to facilitate to exchange of ideas, skills, and experiences fostering on culture of learning and collaboration" [002/2026 §18].

- The body corporate may "organize knowledge sharing activities such as lectures, seminars, trainings and conferences" for persons in Sri Lanka and abroad, to promote its objects [002/2026 §6(h)].

Caveats: This is the Sri Lanka Institute of Agriculture (Incorporation) Bill (Bill, 2025-12-05); only the definition and enabling power appear in the evidence.

question: According to the proposed Pharmaceutical Society of Sri Lanka law, what authority does the Society have to obtain and manage real or personal assets, and what actions may it take with those assets?
answer:
The Society would be legally capable of taking and holding “any property, movable or immovable” and may sell, mortgage, lease, exchange or otherwise dispose of it, subject to written law, the Act and rules under section 7 [047/2026 §13].

- It may “purchase, rent construct, renovate and otherwise obtain lands or buildings” and deal with or dispose of them as the Council determines [047/2026 §6(a)].
- It may undertake or administer lawful trusts or property with similar objects [047/2026 §6(f)].
- Its moneys and property must be applied “solely towards the promotion of the objects” and not paid to members as dividend, bonus or profit [047/2026 §14].

question: In the Institute of Real Estate Professionals, who chairs the Membership and Policy Advisory committees, and how are chairs selected for the remaining committees?
answer:
The President of the Institute chairs both the Membership Committee and the Policy Advisory and Constitutional Committee [656/2025 §18].

- For the remaining committees, each must include at least one Council member, and that member is the Chairman [656/2025 §18].
- Where more than one Council member is appointed to a committee, the Council appoints one of them as Chairperson [656/2025 §18].

question: Under the amended Colombo Port City Economic Commission law, how is the income tax treatment of workers hired by licensed businesses affected depending on whether the licence was granted before or after the new provisions take effect?
answer:
For pre-commencement licensees, employment income of both resident and non-resident employees is “exempt from income tax” for “a period of three years” from the month after the section commences; for licensees granted on/after commencement, such income “shall be liable to income tax” [654/2025 §3].

- Resident employees’ exempt income is “deemed to be a permissible credit to a personal foreign currency account” [654/2025 §3].
- Non-resident employees are also not liable to Sri Lankan income tax on income earned outside Sri Lanka [654/2025 §3].
- Pre-commencement employees must be remunerated in a “designated foreign currency, other than in Sri Lanka Rupees” [654/2025 §3].

question: Under the proposed amendment to the Licensing of Shipping Agents, Freight Forwarders, Non‑Vessel Operating Common Carriers and Container Operators Act, how is the Act’s long title changed regarding the mention of container operators?
answer:
The long title of the principal Act (No. 10 of 1972) is amended by deleting the words "AND CONTAINER OPERATORS", so it reads "FREIGHT FORWARDERS AND NON-VESSEL OPERATING COMMON CARRIERS" [005/2026 §2].

- The same substitution pattern is applied to references in the principal enactment and other written law, and existing documents are read accordingly [005/2026 §3].
- The definition of "container operators" in section 15 is deleted [005/2026 §4], with pending applications and subsisting licences deemed to fall under the Licensing of Container Depot Operators Act, No. 2026 [005/2026 §5].

Caveats: This is the Bill version dated 2026-01-20; no Gazette (GS) version appears in the evidence.

question: Under the proposed amendment to the Convention on the Suppression of Terrorist Financing Act, what modification is being made to the existing law?
answer:
The Bill amends the Convention on the Suppression of Terrorist Financing Act, No. 25 of 2005 by substituting words and provisions in specified sections per a Schedule, and by repealing/replacing several sections [029/2026 §2].

- Extraterritorial reach: new section 2A(2) applies the Act to offences committed "wholly or partly outside Sri Lanka" directed at or resulting in terrorist acts in Sri Lanka, against a Sri Lankan citizen, against a government facility, or to compel the Government [029/2026 §3].
- New offence in section 3(2B) covering collecting/providing funds for terrorist training, travel to commit a terrorist act or to become a "foreign terrorist fighter", and trafficking of persons for terrorist training, with penalty extended to "a fine not exceeding one hundred million rupees" [029/2026 §4].
- Freezing orders: "seven days" becomes "fourteen working days" and "three months" becomes "six months" [029/2026 §5, §6]; High Court may sanction essential transactions (new s.4C) [029/2026 §7].
- New investigative powers (surveillance, undercover operations, controlled deliveries, computer access) and joint investigation teams in new sections 4J and 4K [029/2026 §12].
- Definitions updated, including "foreign terrorist fighter" and "virtual asset", and "terrorist" extended to a foreign terrorist fighter [029/2026 §16].

Caveats: This is the Gazette-published Bill of 2026-04-09; committee-stage amendments are not in the evidence, and the full Schedule substitutions are not reproduced.

question: Which 2025 bill outlines the government's budget and borrowing provisions for the financial year 2026?
answer:
The **Appropriation Bill 2025** (presented 26 September 2025) is the bill that sets the Government’s expenditure and borrowing framework for the “financial year 2026” [639/2025 §1] [639/2025 §2].

- It authorises estimated Government expenditure of “rupees four thousand four hundred thirty-four billion three hundred fifty-six million four hundred sixty-eight thousand” for 2026 [639/2025 §2(1)].
- It authorises 2026 borrowing, with outstanding borrowing not exceeding “rupees three thousand eight hundred billion” [639/2025 §2(1)].

question: What 2026 legislation establishes a new foundation to promote economic growth and rural resource development in Sri Lanka?
answer:
The **Economic and Rural Recourses Development Foundation (Incorporation)** Bill (Bill, 2026-07-27) — it incorporates the Foundation as a body corporate with perpetual succession [055/2026 §2(1)].

- Its stated objects are to develop and modernise economic sectors and to support rural human-resource, micro-entrepreneurship and community programmes [055/2026 §3(1)(a),(b),(g),(h)].
- It is deemed a Voluntary Social Service Organization under Act No. 31 of 1980 [055/2026 §2(2)].

Caveats: The bill title uses "Recourses" while the body text uses "Resources"; only the presented Bill (not a GS version) is in the evidence.

question: Under the proposed Chartered Institute of Media law, what is the maximum length of a suspension the Council can impose instead of disenrolling a member?
answer:
The maximum is **one year**: instead of disenrolling a member found guilty of professional misconduct, the Council may "warn, reprimand or suspend him from membership for such period not exceeding one year" [054/2026 §24].

- The guilt finding must first come from the Disciplinary Committee's report to the Council [054/2026 §23(3)].
- The Council retains discretion to re-enrol a person it considers "fit to become a member" [054/2026 §24].

Caveats: Evidence is from the Bill version (2026-07-22) of the Establishment of the Chartered Institute of Media Bill; no Gazette (GS) version is in the corpus.

question: Under the Protection of Occupants Bill, how long must someone have continuously and peacefully occupied a premises to be regarded as an “occupant”?
answer: More than **three months** of "undisturbed and uninterrupted occupation" of the premises, prior to the events in sections 3, 4 or 5, and the occupation must be lawful. [004/2026 §2]

question: Under the proposed Gambling Regulatory Authority law, what is the age limit beyond which a person cannot serve on the Authority's Board?
answer:
A person "over seventy years of age" is disqualified from appointment as a member of the Board [613/2025 §9(i)].

- The disqualification is listed with other grounds such as being a Member of Parliament, an undischarged insolvent, or holding an interest in gambling [613/2025 §9(a)–(h)].
- Appointed members otherwise hold office for "three years" and may be re-appointed for "not more than two further terms" [613/2025 §10].

Caveats: This is from the Bill version (17 June 2025) of the Gambling Regulatory Authority Bill; only the disqualification at appointment is stated — the text does not expressly address a member reaching 70 while in office.

question: Under the proposed amendment to the Financial Transactions Reporting Act, what is the longest jail term a person can receive for arriving in or departing Sri Lanka with cash or bearer‑negotiable instruments above the minister‑set limit?
answer:
The longest jail term is **one year**: a person convicted by a Magistrate is liable to imprisonment “for a term not exceeding one year”, or a fine up to three times the value, or both [030/2026 §31].

- This applies to arriving in or leaving Sri Lanka with cash or bearer negotiable instruments above the Minister-specified sum without first reporting it [030/2026 §31].

question: Under the proposed Sri Lanka Cricket law, what penalty amount does a member owe if they fail to pay the subscription by the deadline?
answer:
A defaulting member must pay a "late payment fee equal to twice the annual subscription" [077/2026 §30].

- The subscription is due "on or before the thirty first day of December of the year immediately preceding the relevant year"; the doubled late fee is payable by 30 April of the following year [077/2026 §30(3)–(4)].
- If unpaid by that due date, the member "shall automatically forfeit its voting right"; six months later it is removed from the Register of Members [077/2026 §30(5)–(6)].

Caveats: This is the Bill version (Sri Lanka Cricket, 2026-10-06, p.32); no Gazette (GS) version appears in the evidence.

question: Under the proposed Indira Cancer Charitable Trust Act, on which day must the newly formed body corporate settle the Trust's existing debts and liabilities?
answer:
The bill fixes no payment day: it says only that “all debts and liabilities of the Trust existing on the day immediately preceding the date of commencement of this Act, shall be paid by the body corporate hereby constituted” [014/2026 §12].

- The trigger is the eve of commencement — liabilities “existing on” that day pass to the body corporate [014/2026 §12].
- Likewise “all debts due to and subscriptions and contributions payable to the Trust on that day shall be paid to the body corporate” [014/2026 §12].

Caveats: No timeframe for actual settlement appears in the Bill (Indira Cancer Charitable Trust (Incorporation) — Bill, 2026-02-17); committee-stage amendments are not in this corpus.

question: Under the proposed Immigration Bill, what is the minimum and maximum penalty imposed on a ship's master or aircraft captain who fails to report a transit passenger or crew member that appears to have stayed in Sri Lanka?
answer: Under the Immigration Bill (2026-10-07), the penalty is a fine of **not less than Rs. 100,000 and not more than Rs. 500,000**, with the master/captain/agent jointly and severally liable [082/2026 §90].

question: Under the proposed Convention against Doping in Sport amendment, how long does the Board Chairman serve?
answer: The amendment provides that the Board Chairman “shall hold office for a term of three years” and is eligible for reappointment [636/2025 §11]. This is in the Convention against Doping in Sport (Amendment) Bill dated 2025-09-12.

question: Under the amended Rubber Control Act, who is defined as the “Director‑General”?
answer:
The bill substitutes the definition in section 52 of the principal Act: "Director-General" means "the Director-General of the Rubber Development Department, appointed or deemed to have been appointed under this Act" [620/2025 §6].

- This bill is titled "Rubber Control (Amendment) - Bill" (Bill, 2025-07-09) [620/2025 §1], which matches your question.
- The same clause repeals the old "Controller" definition [620/2025 §6], consistent with the Act-wide renaming of "Controller"/"Rubber Controller" to "Director-General" [620/2025 §2].

Caveats: Only the presented Bill version (2025-07-09) is in evidence; no Gazette version or committee amendments are included.

question: In the amended Personal Data Protection Act, which bodies are regarded as a public authority?
answer:
Under the Bill, “public authority” means “a Ministry, any Department or Provincial Council, local authority, or a Ministry or Department of Provincial Council” [591/2025 §13].

- It expressly excludes “a public corporation” and “a company incorporated under the Companies Act, No. 07 of 2007” [591/2025 §13].
- This is a substituted definition in the Personal Data Protection (Amendment) Bill dated 2025-05-08 [591/2025 §13].

question: What criteria does the amendment set for a crop to be classified as an Export Agricultural Crop?
answer:
Under the Promotion of Export Agriculture (Amendment) Bill, a crop must have “export potential in addition to the local consumption,” be declared by the Minister as a “notified agricultural crop” under section 2, and not be an excluded crop [060/2026 §5].

- Excluded: “paddy, vegetables, fruits, root crops and additional food crops belonging to the category of food crops” [060/2026 §5].
- Plantation crops are expressly excluded: “shall not include any crop identified as a plantation crop” [060/2026 §5].

question: Under the proposed Chiththa Advanced Psychological Studies Open Institute of Sri Lanka law, what does the term “qualified auditor” refer to?
answer:
“Qualified auditor” means either an individual accountant or an accounting firm meeting the stated professional membership and practice-certificate requirements [608/2025 §10].

- An individual must be a member of the Institute of Chartered Accountants of Sri Lanka “or any other institute established by law” and possess a certificate to practice issued by that Council [608/2025 §10].
- A firm qualifies if each resident partner meets the same membership and certificate-of-practice requirement [608/2025 §10].

question: Under the proposed Proceeds of Crime Bill, what types of advanced investigative methods can an investigation officer employ with a magistrate’s permission?
answer:
Under the Proceeds of Crime Bill (Bill, 2025-03-01), an investigation officer may use these advanced techniques only with a Magistrate’s judicial authorization [572/2025 §60(1)]:

- Controlled delivery; digital surveillance, including interception and recording of digital, voice and video communications; undercover operations including decoys [572/2025 §60(1)].
- Laying traps; and forensic extraction of data, information and images from computers, mobile phones, digital storage devices and other digital equipment [572/2025 §60(1)].
- Before authorising, the Magistrate must consider “necessity and justification” and “proportionality” [572/2025 §60(3)].

question: Under the proposed Chartered Institute of Media Professionals of Sri Lanka law, how many council members must be present, and must the Chairperson be among them, to constitute a quorum for a council meeting?
answer: A quorum is **“five members including the Chairperson”** [050/2026 §7(2)]. So the Chairperson must be among those present for the Council meeting to be quorate.

question: Under the National Transport Commission amendment, what steps must the Commission and transport operators follow to set and show fares for bus and other transport services?
answer:
Under the **National Transport Commission (Amendment) - Bill (Bill, 2025-05-08)**, the Commission sets fares by formula and Gazette Order, while permit holders must publish and display the applicable fare list.

- The Commission computes fares “in accordance with the formula determined by the Commission … adhering to the national policy … approved by Parliament, and specified by Order published in the Gazette” [592/2025 §19].
- The Commission must publish fare lists on its official website; each provider must prepare its list “in accordance with such lists” and display it “at any conspicuous place of the transportation vehicle” [592/2025 §19].
- The Commission may inspect compliance, and failure is “guilty of an offence under section 40” [592/2025 §19].

question: According to the proposed Mass Foundation law, what continuous legal identity will the foundation have, what ability does it have to bring or face lawsuits, how can it manage its seal, and how is it classified for regulatory oversight?
answer:
The bill gives the Foundation **perpetual succession** under the name “Mass Foundation,” with power to **sue and be sued** [037/2026 §2(1)].

- Its seal may be used only in the presence of **two Committee members**, who must sign independently; custody lies with an office bearer chosen by the Committee [037/2026 §15(1)-(2)].
- It is deemed a **Voluntary Social Service Organization** under the Voluntary Social Service Organizations (Registration and Supervision) Act, No. 31 of 1980, whose provisions apply to management of its affairs [037/2026 §2(2)].

question: Under the amendment to the National Water Supply and Drainage Board Law, when a water supply and sewerage undertaking of an industrial park is transferred to the Board, which minister is treated as the ‘Minister in charge of the subject of Local Government’ for applying Part III of the Act?
answer:
For an industrial park, Part III references to the “Minister in charge of the subject of Local Government” are read as the Minister assigned the subject of the Board of Investment of Sri Lanka, or the Minister assigned the subject of industries, under Article 44 or 45 of the Constitution, “as the case may be” [053/2026 §10(a)].

- This applies to a “water supply and sewerage undertakings of an industrial estate or industrial park” [053/2026 §10(a)].
- Source bill: National Water Supply and Drainage Board (Amendment) - Bill, dated 2026-07-21 [053/2026 §10].

Caveats: The clause does not specify which of the two ministers applies in a given case; it says “as the case may be.”

question: Under the proposed Protection of the State from Terrorism Bill, what responsibilities does a magistrate have when an approved detention centre lies within his jurisdiction?
answer:
Under the bill, the Magistrate for the area where an approved place of detention is located must inspect it "once a month", "without giving any advance notice to the authority in charge" [078/2026 §33(1)].

- On each visit he must "interview the suspects and look into their well-being" and "call for and inspect detention registers, Detention Orders and other books and documents" [078/2026 §33(1)]; the detention authority must give "prompt and unimpeded access" [078/2026 §33(3)].
- If he observes or is told of torture or "cruel, inhuman or degrading treatment", he must "forthwith" order examination by a Judicial Medical Officer and report to him [078/2026 §33(4)–(5)], acting in terms of section 31 [078/2026 §31(1)].
- Where the place fails the humane-treatment requirements, the fact is to be "informed to the Inspector General of Police" [078/2026 §34(2)].

Caveats: This is the Bill version (2026-10-06); the Magistrate before whom the suspect was first produced also holds these powers [078/2026 §33(2)].

question: Under the Mediation (Civil and Commercial Disputes) Bill, which civil or commercial disagreements can be taken to mediation and which types are excluded from this law?
answer:
The Bill covers "civil and commercial disputes" mediated under a mediation agreement, by voluntary referral, or by court referral [622/2025 §2], but excludes matters governed by the older mediation statutes and disputes that only a court decree can settle [622/2025 §2] [622/2025 §3].

- Excluded: disputes required to be mediated under the Mediation Boards Act, No. 72 of 1988 or the Mediation (Special Categories of Disputes) Act, No. 21 of 2003 [622/2025 §2].
- Excluded: disputes whose settlement "requires the inclusion of terms that can be given effect to only on a decree or order of court," including the schedule list — divorce, nullity, minors/persons of unsound mind, adoption, probate, insolvency, admiralty rights in rem, fundamental rights [622/2025 §3] [622/2025 §30].
- For such excluded matters, related matters may still be mediated to submit settlement terms to court [622/2025 §3].

Caveats: Only the Bill version (11 July 2025) is in evidence; no Gazette version to compare.

question: What audit regulations govern the financial statements of Samurdhi community‑based banking societies under the Samurdhi amendment?
answer:
Under the **Samurdhi (Amendment) Bill (2025-06-17)**, the audit of accounts of Samurdhi community based banking societies is governed by Article 154 of the Constitution on public corporation audits and by the **National Audit Act, No. 19 of 2018** [614/2025 §3].

- New section **35A** applies those audit provisions to “samurdhi community based banking societies” [614/2025 §3].
- The same audit regime is applied separately to samurdhi community based **banks** under new section 28A [614/2025 §2].

Caveat: the text speaks of “accounts,” not “financial statements”; no other audit regulations are given in the evidence.

question: Under the proposed Companies (Amendment) Act, what remedy is available to a company whose name has been struck off, and what are the effects on its former assets?
answer:
Under the Companies (Amendment) Bill (Bill, 2025-06-05) [606/2025 §17], a struck-off company may apply to court before the expiry of "ten years from the date of operation" of the Act, making the Attorney-General a party, to show cause why it could not comply; the court may then permit re-registration and "make an order for the return to the company of all property previously vested in the State".

- Third-party rights acquired in good faith from the State are "not be affected in any manner" [606/2025 §17].
- If property was destroyed, damaged, or never taken into State possession, "the State shall not be liable to any party" [606/2025 §17].

Caveats: This is a Bill version, not a Gazette version, and committee-stage amendments are not included.

question: Under the revised Anti‑Corruption Act, in what situations will a person charged with a corruption offence be refused bail?
answer:
Under the bill, bail is refused where the bribe solicited, accepted or offered is "not less than one hundred thousand rupees", or where the corruption caused the Government a loss, or gained a benefit, favour or advantage, of "not less than five hundred thousand rupees" — the value being confirmed by the Director-General by certificate [063/2026 §17].

- Such a suspect or accused "shall not be granted bail except in exceptional circumstances by a High Court" [063/2026 §17].
- Generally all offences under the Act are "cognizable and non-bailable as per the provisions of the Bail Act, No. 30 of 1997", subject to the above proviso [063/2026 §17].

Caveats: This is the Anti-Corruption (Amendment) Bill of 2026-08-19 (Bill version), amending section 149 of Act No. 9 of 2023; no Gazette version is in the evidence.

question: Under the proposed Prevention of Foreign Terrorist Fighters law, how are offences listed in Part B of the extradition schedule treated when Sri Lanka considers extraditing a suspect to another UN member state?
answer:
Under clause 11, such offences are deemed **not** to be "an offence of a political character or an offence connected with a political offence or an offence inspired by political motives" — but only for the purposes of extradition (and assistance under clause 12) between Sri Lanka and a UN Member State [085/2026 §11].

- This applies "notwithstanding anything in the Extradition Law, No. 8 of 1977" [085/2026 §11].
- The deeming is expressly limited: "for the purposes only of extradition ... as between the Government of Sri Lanka and any UN Member State or of affording assistance to a UN Member State under section 12" [085/2026 §11].
- Clause 8 separately inserts an offence under this Act into the Extradition Law Schedule "immediately before Part B" [085/2026 §8].

Caveats: The bill is the Bill version dated 2026-10-20; only clauses 8 and 11 touch this, and neither defines what "Part B" itself contains.

question: Under the revised National Environmental Act, what monetary penalty does a person face if convicted of an offence covered by Section 23r, and what extra daily charge applies if the violation persists after the conviction?
answer:
Under the National Environmental (Amendment) Bill (2026-05-06), a person convicted under amended section 23r(2) faces a fine of “not less than one hundred thousand rupees and not more than one million rupees” [032/2026 §18].

- If the offence continues after conviction, an additional fine of “five thousand rupees for each day” applies [032/2026 §18].

question: What penalty does the amendment to the National Audit Act impose for the offence covered by Section 42?
answer:
The amendment sets the penalty under section 42 to “a fine not exceeding one hundred thousand rupees or to an imprisonment of either description for a term not exceeding one year or to both such fine and imprisonment” [619/2025 §13].

- This replaces the previous “fine not less than five thousand rupees and not more than twenty five thousand rupees” [619/2025 §13].
- The bill is the National Audit (Amendment) - Bill dated 2025-07-08 [619/2025 §1].

Caveat: the evidence gives the penalty but not the conduct constituting the section 42 offence.

question: Under the proposed Elimination of Rabies and Registration of Dogs law, what fine and additional action apply if a dog owner does not vaccinate and register the dog after being given a notice?
answer:
Under the Bill, the owner becomes liable to a penalty of "two thousand rupees" in addition to the registration fee payable under section 5, and the local authority must itself vaccinate and register the dog in the Register of Dogs [076/2026 §7(4)].

- The notice gives fourteen days, which the authorised officer may extend "for further fourteen days" for a reasonable cause [076/2026 §7(2)–(3)].
- Registration itself is with the relevant local authority "on payment of a prescribed fee" [076/2026 §5(1)].

Caveats: this is the Bill version (2026-09-24); no Gazette (GS) version appears in the evidence, and the penalty applies on failure to comply with the notice rather than on conviction.

question: Under the proposed amendment to Sri Lanka’s drug control law, how is the list of named narcotics changed and what new penalty is introduced for manufacturing other listed dangerous drugs?
answer:
The Bill adds "methamphetamine" to the named narcotics in sections 54A(1)(a) and 54AA(1), and inserts a new paragraph (aa) creating a separate offence of manufacturing the other dangerous drugs listed in Groups A–E of Part I of the Third Schedule [068/2026 §2] [068/2026 §3].

- Conviction is "by the High Court without a jury" [068/2026 §2].
- Penalty: a fine "not less than two hundred thousand rupees and not exceeding five hundred thousand rupees", or imprisonment "not less than ten years and not exceeding twenty years", or both [068/2026 §2].
- The new offence expressly excludes heroin, cocaine, morphine, opium and methamphetamine [068/2026 §2].

Caveats: This is the Poisons, Opium and Dangerous Drugs (Amendment) Bill (2026-09-08); only the presented Bill text is in evidence, not any Gazette version.

question: Under the proposed Presidents' Entitlements repeal, will former presidents or their widows keep receiving housing, regular payments, secretarial assistance, official transport or a widow's pension once the new law takes effect?
answer:
No. From the date the new law commences, those benefits "shall no longer be provided with or paid to": residences/monthly allowances, secretarial allowance, official transport and other facilities, and a widow's monthly pension [627/2025 §3].

- The underlying Presidents' Entitlements Act, No. 4 of 1986 is repealed [627/2025 §2].
- The cessation expressly covers benefits received "preceding the date of commencement of this Act" [627/2025 §3].
- Only pre-existing entitlements under sections 2, 3 and 4 of the repealed Act are listed; the text says nothing about other facilities [627/2025 §3].

Caveats: This is the Bill as presented 2025-08-07; committee-stage amendments are not in the corpus.

question: Under the proposed amendment to the Penal Code, what new penalty is introduced for intentionally causing serious injury to a child under 18?
answer:
The Bill introduces section 316a: “voluntarily” causing grievous hurt to a person under 18 is punishable with imprisonment of either description “which may extend to ten years”, and the offender “shall also be liable to fine” [630/2025 §6].

- The court may also order compensation after considering a victim impact statement from the National Authority [630/2025 §6].
- This does not apply to cases covered by section 326 [630/2025 §6].

Caveat: the text says “voluntarily”, not “intentionally”; the “wilfully” to “intentionally” change is in section 308a only [630/2025 §3].

question: How does the proposed amendment to the Social Security Contribution Levy Act change the turnover limits and the applicable dates in Section 5, and what new limit is introduced for periods starting on 1 April 2026?
answer:
The amendment re-dates Section 5(1)'s existing turnover thresholds and adds a new four-quarter threshold of “thirty-six million rupees” for periods from 1 April 2026 [023/2026 §3].

- Paragraph (c) is limited to turnover “on or after January 1, 2024 and prior to April 1, 2026”, with the “sixty million rupees” figure retained but its trailing “or” removed [023/2026 §3(2)]; paragraph (b) likewise only drops “or” after “hundred and twenty million rupees” [023/2026 §3(1)].
- New paragraph (d): for any period “commencing on or after April 1, 2026”, the test is whether aggregate turnover over “consecutive four quarters” does not exceed thirty-six million rupees [023/2026 §3(3)].
- This is the Social Security Contribution Levy (Amendment) Bill, 2026-03-17 (Bill version) [023/2026 §1].

Caveats: §3's text is garbled at the proviso, so which exact consequence (e.g. exemption vs. deregistration) attaches to the new limit is not clear from the passage.

question: What changes does the amendment to Section 14 of the Sri Lanka Electricity Act make to the ownership percentage requirement and to the type of entities mentioned in its subsections?
answer:
The amendment to Section 14 changes the ownership threshold from “more than fifty per centum” to “one hundred per centum,” and replaces references to a “person” with a “company incorporated in terms of the Companies Act, No. 07 of 2007” [599/2025 §12].

- Subsection (1): “more than fifty per centum” is substituted with “one hundred per centum” [599/2025 §12].
- Subsection (2): “Any person who” becomes “Any company incorporated in terms of the Companies Act, No. 07 of 2007, which” [599/2025 §12].
- Subsection (3): “a person who” becomes “a company, which” [599/2025 §12].

Caveats: The evidence does not describe the substantive purpose of Section 14 beyond these textual substitutions.

question: Under the proposed amendment to the Trusts Ordinance, which part of Section 3 is being removed and how is the definition of “express trust” being changed?
answer:
The bill amends section 3 of the Trusts Ordinance by repealing paragraph (n) and by narrowing the wording in the "express trust" definition in paragraph (p) [086/2026 §2].

- Paragraph **(n)** of section 3 is repealed outright — the text does not say what that paragraph dealt with [086/2026 §2].
- In paragraph (p), the definition of "express trust" substitutes "trust in the form" for "trust generally in the form" [086/2026 §2].

Caveats: Evidence is from the Trusts (Amendment) Bill (Bill, 2026-10-21); the substance of the repealed paragraph (n) is not stated, and the point is introduced as a further amendment to the Ordinance "as last amended by Act, No. 6 of 2018" [086/2026 §2].

question: Under the proposed amendment to the Judicature Act, how are the retirement ages for judges and magistrates being changed?
answer:
The Bill raises the age in section 6(3) from "sixty-one years" to "sixty-three years", and replaces section 6(4) so that "the age of retirement of all other Judges and Magistrates shall be sixty-two years" [064/2026 §3].

- The new 62-year rule applies "Notwithstanding anything to the contrary in the Public and Judicial Officers (Retirement) Ordinance (Chapter 355)" [064/2026 §3].
- Both changes are made to the Judicature Act, No. 2 of 1978 ("the principal enactment") [064/2026 §2].

Caveats: The Bill (Judicature (Amendment), dated 2026-08-18) does not state in these passages which category of judges section 6(3) covers, so I cannot say which judges get 63.

question: Under the proposed amendment to the Universities Act, how many terms is a person allowed to serve as dean of a faculty?
answer:
A person may be appointed Dean of a Faculty for **no more than two terms**: “No person shall be appointed as the Dean of a Faculty for more than two terms” [655/2025 §2].

- This is a new subsection (4) added to section 49 of the Universities Act [655/2025 §2].

question: What 2025 legislation establishes the professional facilities‑management institute as a legal corporate body in Sri Lanka?
answer:
The bill is the **Institute of Facilities Management Sri Lanka (Incorporation)** — Bill, 2025-08-06 — which refers throughout to "the body corporate" and vests it with powers, funds and rules.

- Its Council, on the body corporate's behalf, sets membership criteria and fees [628/2025 §1]; the body corporate holds its own fund and keeps audited accounts [628/2025 §2].
- Membership grades carry protected designations, e.g. "F.IFMSL" and "C.FM.", with a bar on unregistered use of "Chartered Facility Manager" [628/2025 §1].
- A Membership Affairs Board registers Chartered Facility Managers, deciding applications within "not more than one month" [628/2025 §2].

Caveats: the evidence does not quote the incorporation/enacting clause itself, so the exact section constituting the corporation cannot be cited; no Gazette (GS) version appears here.

question: Which 2025 legislation creates a legal corporation for the charitable foundation named after senior monk Mabotuwana Sri Piyarathana Nayaka Thero?
answer:
The Mabotuwana Sri Piyarathana Nayaka Thero Suwasevana Foundation (Incorporation) Bill, dated 2025-05-08 (Bill 596/2025), is the one — it constitutes the Foundation's members as a "body corporate with perpetual succession" [596/2025 §2].

- Short title: "Mabotuwana Sri Piyarathana Nayaka Thero Suwasevana Foundation (Incorporation) Act, No. of 2025" [596/2025 §1].
- It may sue and be sued, and have a common seal [596/2025 §2].
- Objects focus on residential and support facilities for patients at the Karapitiya Hospital [596/2025 §3].

Caveats: This is the Bill as presented (2025-05-08), not the enacted Act; the Act number is left blank.

question: What 2026 amendment revises the Act that governs marriage and divorce among the Kandyan community (Chapter 113)?
answer:
The evidence identifies the **Kandyan Marriage and Divorce (Amendment) Bill** dated **2026-02-19** as the 2026 amendment bill. [016/2026 §1]

- It amends section 32 by substituting paragraph (a) with “Adultery by the husband or wife after marrige” and repealing paragraph (b). [016/2026 §2]
- It states that in any Sinhala/Tamil inconsistency, the Sinhala text prevails. [016/2026 §3]

Caveats: The evidence does not mention “Chapter 113,” so I cannot confirm that reference from the passages provided.

question: What is the 2026 legislation that establishes the Al‑Hashimi Association as a legal corporate entity?
answer:
The matching 2026 Bill is the **Al‑Hashimi Association (Incorporation) Bill** (Bill, 2026‑05‑21). Its clause 2 would constitute members as a body corporate with “perpetual succession” under the name “Al‑Hashimi Association” [039/2026 §2].

- Short title: “Al-Hashimi Association (Incorporation) Act, No. of 2026” [039/2026 §1].
- It may “sue and be sued” and use a common seal [039/2026 §2].

Caveat: the evidence is the Bill version, not an enacted Act; commencement is stated as “from and after the date of commencement” [039/2026 §2].

question: Which 2026 bill repeals the 2009 act that created the position of chief of the defence staff in Sri Lanka?
answer:
The Chief of Defence Staff (Repeal) Bill (Bill, 2026-08-04) repeals the Chief of Defence Staff Act, No. 35 of 2009 [059/2026 §2].

- On commencement, the Chief of Defence Staff and Committee members "cease to hold such office" [059/2026 §3(1)].
- Staff are reassigned to the armed forces, Police, Civil Security Department or public service; assets transfer to the Defence Ministry [059/2026 §3(2)].
- Pending suits continue "as if there had been no such repeal" [059/2026 §3(2)(c)].

Caveats: Only the Bill (presented) version appears here; no Gazette version.

question: What 2025 legislation modifies the 1988 Provincial Councils Elections Act in Sri Lanka?
answer:
The 2025 Bill is the **Provincial Councils Elections (Amendment) - Bill** (dated 2025-06-05), which amends the Provincial Councils Elections Act, No. 2 of 1988 [605/2025 §1].

- It makes the 1988 Act provisions “in force on September 21, 2017” operative from commencement, notwithstanding amendments by Act, No. 17 of 2017 [605/2025 §2].
- It preserves acts done from 22 September 2017 to commencement if not inconsistent with the 1988 Act [605/2025 §2].

Caveats: The evidence identifies a Bill, not an enacted Act.

question: Which 2025 bill amends the 2016 Act that provides a financial assistance scheme for workers?
answer:
The **Budgetary Relief Allowance of Workers (Amendment) Bill** (Bill, 3 June 2025) amends the **Budgetary Relief Allowance of Workers Act, No. 4 of 2016** [602/2025 §2].

- It substitutes periods ending **“March 31, 2025”** in sections 3(1) and 3(2) of the 2016 Act [602/2025 §2].
- The amendment is deemed to have come into operation on **April 1, 2025** [602/2025 §1].

question: Which 2025 bill seeks to amend the 2016 legislation that establishes the minimum wage for employees in Sri Lanka?
answer:
The **National Minimum Wage of Workers (Amendment) Bill** (Bill, 3 June 2025) amends the National Minimum Wage of Workers Act, No. 3 of 2016 [604/2025 §2].

- It replaces minimum wage levels, setting “twenty-seven thousand rupees” monthly from 1 April 2025 and “thirty thousand rupees” from 1 January 2026 [604/2025 §2].
- It deems the Act operative from 1 April 2025 [604/2025 §1].

question: Which 2025 amendment alters the 2005 law that established the workers' special financial assistance allowance?
answer:
The **Budgetary Relief Allowance of Workers (Amendment) Bill** (Bill, 3 June 2025) amends the **Budgetary Relief Allowance of Workers Act, No. 36 of 2005** [603/2025 §2].

- It substitutes the original “With effect from August 1, 2005” wording with “For the period commencing on August 1, 2005 and ending on March 31, 2025” in section 3(1) [603/2025 §2].
- The amendment is deemed to have come into operation on **April 1, 2025** [603/2025 §1(2)].

Caveats: The evidence calls it “Budgetary Relief Allowance,” not “special financial assistance allowance.”

question: What 2026 legislation proposes to abolish the 1977 law that provided retirement benefits to Sri Lankan parliamentarians?
answer:
The **Parliamentary Pensions (Repeal) Bill** (Bill, 2026-01-07) — it expressly repeals the Parliamentary Pensions Law, No. 1 of 1977 [001/2026 §2].

- Anyone already receiving a pension under that Law (or s.9 of Act No. 1 of 1982 / Act No. 47 of 1990) "cease[s] to receive such pension" from the date the Act commences [001/2026 §3].
- Short title: "Parliamentary Pensions (Repeal) Act, No. of 2026" [001/2026 §1].
- In any Sinhala/Tamil inconsistency, the Sinhala text prevails [001/2026 §4].

Caveats: Only the presented Bill version is in evidence; no Gazette (GS) version is given, and no commencement date is stated.

question: Which 2025 bill sought to modify the 1988 Sri Lankan law that imposes a tax on gambling activities?
answer:
The **Betting and Gaming Levy (Amendment) Bill** (Bill, 2025-10-21) sought to amend the Betting and Gaming Levy Act, No. 40 of 1988 [642/2025 §2].

- It added an 18% rate for years commencing on or after October 1, 2025 [642/2025 §2(1)(c)].
- It raised the relevant fee from “United States Dollars fifty” to “United States Dollars one hundred” [642/2025 §2(2)].

question: Which 2025 bill proposes changes to the Land Development Ordinance (Chapter 464)?
answer:
The **Land Development (Amendment) Bill** (Bill, presented 22 July 2025) is the 2025 bill amending the Land Development enactment [625/2025 §1].

- It repeals "or upon his or her marriage" in subsection 48A 2(c) of the principal enactment [625/2025 §2].
- It repeals subsection 48B 1(a) [625/2025 §3].
- It amends section 68(1), substituting "fails without reasonable cause to succeed" for "fails to succeed" [625/2025 §4].

Caveats: the evidence only calls it the "principal enactment" and never cites "Ordinance (Chapter 464)", so that identification is unconfirmed.

question: Which 2026 bill updates the 2018 Finance Act No. 35?
answer:
The **Finance (Amendment) Bill** (Bill, 6 May 2026) updates the Finance Act, No. 35 of 2018 by amending its section 44 [034/2026 §2].

- It inserts a five-year exemption from the levy for newly constructed cellular towers commencing commercial operations on or after 1 January 2026 [034/2026 §2(1)].
- It makes payment of the levy “[s]ubject to the provisions of subsection (1)” [034/2026 §2(2)].

question: Which 2026 bill revises the 1956 law that sets rules for female workers, teenage employees and child labor?
answer:
The **Employment of Women, Young Persons and Children (Amendment) Bill** (Bill, 2026-07-22) — it amends the Employment of Women, Young Persons and Children Act, No. 47 of 1956 [056/2026 §2].

- It substitutes "one hundred thousand rupees" for "ten thousand rupees" in sections 7(3), 13(2) and 20a(3) of the principal enactment [056/2026 §2] [056/2026 §3] [056/2026 §4].
- The higher amounts do not apply to offences committed before the Act comes into operation [056/2026 §5].
- In any Sinhala/Tamil inconsistency, the Sinhala text prevails [056/2026 §6].

Caveats: Only the presented Bill (not a Gazette version) is in evidence, and it does not spell out the conduct each amended section penalises.

question: Which 2025 bill proposes to revoke the 2024 legislation that introduced internet safety and content regulation measures?
answer:
The **Online Safety (Repeal) Bill** (Bill, 2025-05-08) proposes repealing the **Online Safety Act, No. 9 of 2024** [590/2025 §2].

- Its short title is the “Online Safety (Repeal) Act” [590/2025 §1].
- Regulations made under the 2024 Act after its enactment would also be repealed from the new Act’s enactment date [590/2025 §3].

question: What 2025 legislation addresses re‑conducting postponed local council elections by allowing new nominations and setting a fresh election date?
answer:
The matching bill is **Local Authorities Elections (Special Provisions)** — Bill [566/2025], dated 2025-01-09, covering the local authorities in its Schedule.

- It voids the earlier nomination papers: they are "deemed to be of no force and effect as if such nomination papers had never been submitted", and the section 38 notices are revoked [566/2025 §2(1)–(2)].
- Fresh steps must commence, with nomination notices under section 26 published on a date the Election Commission determines by Gazette Order, "not later than three months from the date of coming into operation of this Act" [566/2025 §3].
- Deposits by candidates are to be refunded on production of the section 29(3) receipt [566/2025 §2(3)].

Caveats: the bill fixes the *nomination notice* deadline, not a fresh polling date; and it is dated 2025-01-09 yet cited in its long title as "No. of 2024" [566/2025 §1].

question: Which 2025 bill updates the 2008 act that governs major strategic development projects in Sri Lanka?
answer:
The **Strategic Development Projects (Amendment) Bill** (Bill version, dated 2025-11-14) amends the Strategic Development Projects Act, No. 14 of 2008 — [650/2025 §2].

- It cuts the exemption period in section 2 from "twenty-five years" to "ten years" [650/2025 §2].
- It replaces section 3, requiring an ex-ante cost-benefit analysis by the Ministry of Finance, with a recommendation due "within one month" [650/2025 §3].
- Existing tax holidays granted before the amendment continue to be valid for their stated duration [650/2025 §6].

Caveats: Only the Bill (presented) version appears here; no Gazette version is in the evidence, so any GS/Bill differences cannot be checked.

question: Which 2026 bill was introduced to legally establish the UnV charitable foundation?
answer:
It is the **UnV Foundation (Incorporation)** Bill, numbered 010/2026 (Bill version, dated 2026-01-22), which provides for the Foundation to have "perpetual succession" as a body corporate [010/2026 §2].

- It is deemed a Voluntary Social Service Organization under Act No. 31 of 1980 [010/2026 §2].
- Its declared objects include children's education, drug rehabilitation and youth self-employment [010/2026 §3].
- The first Committee must be appointed or elected "within one year" of commencement [010/2026 §5].

Caveats: Only the Bill (presented) version appears here; no Gazette (GS) version is in the evidence.

question: Which 2025 bill updates Sri Lanka's 1979 criminal procedure legislation?
answer:
The **Code of Criminal Procedure (Amendment) Bill** dated **8 April 2025** updates Sri Lanka’s Code of Criminal Procedure Act, No. 15 of 1979 [579/2025 §1][579/2025 §2].

- It inserts new sections 144A and 144B after section 144 of the 1979 Act [579/2025 §2].
- It also amends section 241 and inserts sections 241A and 241B [579/2025 §3][579/2025 §4].
- It further inserts provisions on remote evidence, sections 273A–273U [579/2025 §5].

question: What 2026 bill proposes the twenty‑second revision of Sri Lanka’s constitution?
answer:
The **Twenty Second Amendment to the Constitution — Bill** (Bill, 2026-08-18) is the 2026 bill; its short title is exactly that [065/2026 §1].

- It replaces Article 107(5): Supreme Court judges retire at "sixty-seven years", Court of Appeal judges at "sixty-five years" [065/2026 §2].
- The Chief Justice retires at 67 or on completion of "six years" from appointment, "whichever occurs earlier" [065/2026 §2].
- Article 137 is amended from "not more than nineteen other Judges" to "not more than twenty four other Judges" [065/2026 §3].

Caveats: Only the Bill (presented) version appears here; no Gazette ("GS") version or committee-stage amendments are in the evidence.

question: Which 2026 bill seeks to repeal the 1972 Tenancy Act (No. 7) in Sri Lanka?
answer:
The **Rent (Repeal) - Bill** (Bill, 2026-01-20) — note it is the *Rent* Act, not "Tenancy" Act, that is repealed.

- §2: "The Rent Act, No. 7 of 1972 is hereby repealed." [006/2026 §2]
- §1: it comes into operation on the date the certificate is endorsed under Article 79 ("relevant date"). [006/2026 §1]
- §3: for one year from that date, no ejectment actions against tenants in possession and no rent above the "authorised rent". [006/2026 §3]

Caveats: Only this bill's presented version appears in the evidence; no Gazette (GS) version is included.

question: What 2026 legislation creates a corporate entity for the Mahawilachchiya children’s education centre?
answer:
The 2026 Bill is the **Mahawilachchiya Education Centre for Children (Incorporation) Bill** (Bill, 18 February 2026), which would create a body corporate under that name [015/2026 §1] [015/2026 §2].

- It provides that members “shall hereafter be admitted as members of the body corporate hereby constituted” [015/2026 §2(1)].
- The body corporate has “perpetual succession” and may sue and be sued [015/2026 §2(1)].

Caveats: The evidence is a **Bill**, dated 18 February 2026, not an enacted Act; it also uses a slightly different corporate name in §2.
